name: vibe3d
_comment-toolchain-floor: TASK 2004/2540 -- the project's compiler floor is D frontend >=2.111 (`dmd` 2.111, `ldc` 1.41.0 -- LDC's minor version is not the frontend version; 1.40.0 is frontend 2.110), because six files (source/drag.d, source/math.d, source/tools/create/box.d, source/tools/transform/{move,transform}.d, source/ui/image_rows.d) use `const ref <type> <name> = <expr>;` ref-local declarations, stabilized in that frontend release. Before this field existed, an old compiler picked up by the short name did not refuse by version -- it died on that construct in whichever file the compiler reached first, e.g. `source/ui/image_rows.d(564,9): Error: variable ... - only parameters, functions and foreach declarations can be ref`, read as an unrelated code regression rather than a stale toolchain (this was predicted in this very comment's ancestor and happened anyway, 2026-08-26). `toolchainRequirements` makes dub check the invoked compiler's version BEFORE any source file compiles, so the refusal now names the floor instead of an arbitrary file (mutation verified 2026-08-28: with this field, `dub build --compiler=/usr/bin/ldc2 --build=release --d-version=ReleaseBuild` on the system ldc 1.40.0 refuses immediately with `Error Installed ldc-1.40.0 does not comply with vibe3d compiler requirement: ldc >=1.41.0`; with the field removed the SAME command instead dies mid-compile on the ref-local error above, plus a second, unrelated frontend-version-gated error class -- `dup()` on a `const` associative array not implicitly converting, source/snapshot.d and source/tool_presets.d -- which this field does not name and does not need to, since refusing by version subsumes every frontend-gated construct at once). It does not change which compiler gets picked when the PATH resolves a short name to something below the floor (`/usr/bin/ldc2` on this host is 1.40.0; the project's own is `~/.local/dlang/ldc2-1.42.0-linux-x86_64/bin/ldc2`) -- that is a PATH/session convenience question, deliberately left open here.
_comment-version: MIRROR, not the source of truth. The version the BINARY reports is `appVersion` in packages/application-core/source/app_version.d — a plain D literal, so a clean clone with no git and no network still produces a binary that can name itself. This field exists because it is what `dub describe` and any package consumer read; tests/test_app_version.d fails when the two disagree, and CI's tag check keys off the D literal.
_comment-imgui-flag-boundary: TASK 5930 -- source/imgui_flag_abi.c is ImportC, not a separately configured C build: its flag values are compiled from the cimgui.h shipped by the exact d_imgui package that also supplies the linked archive. The ImportC file must not sort first in dub's source list; putting it first exposed a DMD full-build ordering defect during admission. The D side uses extern(C) integer accessors instead of importing the C module because the latter produced an undefined ModuleInfo link in the full application. Only integer flag constants cross this boundary; no cimgui struct layout does. Every Windows build now requires cl.exe on PATH for ImportC. .github/workflows/build.yml activates the MSVC developer environment before dub, but Windows proof for this boundary is necessarily the post-merge nightly; rollback is git revert of this slice's own commits.
_comment-libs-linux: gdk-3/gobject-2.0 were dropped in task 0431 when the Linux file-dialog backend moved from GTK3 to xdg-desktop-portal (see third_party/nfde): they resolved only nfd_gtk symbols, which are no longer compiled. Keep wayland-client -- NFD's xdg-foreign glue (NFD_WAYLAND=ON) links it, and it was already a DT_NEEDED before this change. dbus-1 (the portal backend's link dep) is declared by third_party/nfde's own libs-linux, not here.
_comment-sdl2-dir: SDL2_DIR selects the matching SDL2 library before D-ImGui's Homebrew search paths. CI sets it to the isolated x64 prefix or the arm64 Homebrew prefix. Local builds without SDL2_DIR continue to use D-ImGui's existing search paths.
description: simple 3d modeller inspired by MODO and LightWave
_comment-stb-image: d-stb-image (task 0662) replaces the vendored third_party/stb_image: the same header, the same #defines, the same CMake build, now a shim like the other D-* packages. Two properties of the move are worth keeping in mind if it is ever reverted. (1) It is a GIT dep, so its C static library is built inside the dub package cache rather than into the workspace -- which means it needs no cache-drop step in .github/workflows the way the nfde PATH dep does, because the D target and the C lib it links are cached together and evicted together, and `git clean` on the workspace cannot desynchronise them. (2) The old package was a `sourceLibrary`, which has no artifact for dub to judge up to date, so its preBuildCommands ran on EVERY build that built anything; the shim is a `staticLibrary`, so dub skips them once its target is current. Neither of those is cosmetic -- see the shim's own dub.json comment for the measurements.
_comment-onnx-per-config: d-onnxruntime (AI candidate ranker backend) is NOT a base dependency — it is added per-configuration alongside the `WithAI` version so the `modeling-noai` build can omit it entirely. onnxruntime.dll statically imports api-ms-win-core-path (Windows 8+), so dropping it is what makes a Windows 7-capable build possible. Only packages/ai-advisor/source/ai/onnx_backend.d touches the binding; all of it is gated by version(WithAI).
_comment-instrumented-buildtypes: TASK 1410 -- the four instrumented buildTypes (check, check-unit, check-release, sanitize) exist so crashes are found by the nightly lane instead of by a user. THE SHIPPED RELEASE DOES NOT READ ANY OF THEM: release is `--build=release`, dub's own built-in buildType, and none of these names appear in it. That is a checkable property, not a promise -- .github/workflows/sanitizer.yaml's preflight runs `dub describe --build=release --compiler=$LDC --config=modeling` and fails if `--fsanitize` or SanitizerSelfTest shows up in targets[].buildSettings.dflags/versions, plus a `strings` check on the release binary for `selftest.fault`. Passing --compiler is not optional there: `dub describe --build=release` with no --compiler defaults to DMD and DROPS every dflags-ldc entry, so the release-untouched mutation would pass vacuously. All four are LDC-ONLY (dmd implements neither --fsanitize nor --checkaction). Use the ABSOLUTE ldc2 path ($HOME/.local/dlang/ldc2-1.42.0-linux-x86_64/bin/ldc2, the same one tools/perf/run.d hardcodes): `--compiler=ldc2` resolves to /usr/bin/ldc2 = LDC 1.40 on this host, which CANNOT build vibe3d at all (it rejects `ref` locals in six pre-existing files), so a lane using the short name would fail on an unrelated compile error and read as `the instrumented build is broken`.
_comment-instrumented-targetname: THE BINARY NAME IS A REAL HAZARD AND `targetName` DOES NOT SOLVE IT -- measured, do not re-attempt. dub.json declares no root targetName, so EVERY buildType writes ./vibe3d, and the nightly perf lane (perf.yaml) runs `run.d frames --no-build` against exactly that path in a workspace deliberately kept unclean (`clean: false`); an instrumented binary left there is read, silently, by the next 03:30 gating run. tools/perf/run.d already carries this trap in its own words (its `NOTE: ./vibe3d is now the perf buildType binary` warnings). The obvious fix -- a per-buildType `targetName` -- was tried here and is INERT: on dub 1.41, `dub describe --build=check` reports `targetName: vibe3d` with the field set, and `dub build --build=check` writes ./vibe3d anyway. The fields were therefore removed rather than left in place looking effective. The working mechanism is explicit and lives in tools/sanitizer/lane.d: `lane.d build <buildType>` builds, immediately renames ./vibe3d to ./vibe3d-<buildType>, and FAILS if ./vibe3d still exists afterwards; `lane.d stage <buildType>` copies it back to ./vibe3d (which run_test.d hardcodes, run_test.d:792) and writes the build stamp; `lane.d teardown` deletes ./vibe3d and fails if it cannot. The workflow's teardown step is `if: always()`.
_comment-instrumented-no-ubsan: THERE IS NO UBSan HERE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Measured on the shipped LDC 1.42.0 tarball: --fsanitize= accepts address, thread, memory, leak, fuzzer and REJECTS undefined, integer, bounds, float-cast-overflow (`Error: Unrecognized -fsanitize value 'undefined'`). The shipped ldc2 carries no UBSan runtime, so the cheapest phase of the original plan has no mechanism at all. The only route to it is rebuilding the runtime with `ldc-build-runtime` (shipped in the same tarball) -- a separate task, deliberately not attempted here. The one UB finding that motivated UBSan (params.d's float->int cast) is covered instead by a BEHAVIOURAL test that needs no sanitizer at all: tests/test_param_cast_overflow.d.
_comment-assimp-static: Interchange owns the native static codec dependency and its unchanged build/link settings. Desktop imports codecs through the package dependency.
_comment-thinlto: DUB applies the root build type to every target, including dependency archives. ThinLTO is scoped to perf and the explicit desktop Build profiles. DUB drops compiler -O3 during a separate link, so each platform also selects LTO O3 at the linker; Linux's explicit plugin option overrides LDC's generated O0. Ordinary debug/release, DMD, perf-count/perf-unit and sanitizer profiles retain their existing flags.

profile-fp._comment: Profiling build: forces frame pointers so perf --call-graph fp produces clean stacks without DWARF unwind cost. Use: `dub build --build=profile-fp` then `perf record -F 999 --call-graph fp -p $(pgrep vibe3d) sleep 5`. DMD uses `-gs`; LDC uses `--frame-pointer=all` (its `-gs` equivalent) — kept separate so the buildType works under either compiler.

perf._comment: Perf-harness build: optimized + inlined release with PerfProbe instrumentation active. releaseMode strips bounds-checks/asserts off the hot per-vertex loops so the timers measure the tool, not bounds-checking. The default build defines no PerfProbe version, so g_perf calls compile to no-ops. Use: `dub build --build=perf --compiler=ldc2`.

perf-count._comment: Debug build with PerfProbe active but no optimizer, for CI counter invariants: counts are control-flow, so ldc/optimize/stable hardware are unnecessary. dmd-buildable. Default build defines no PerfProbe, so this never affects it.

perf-unit._comment: PerfProbe module-unittest build. Like check-unit, this explicitly keeps both `unittests` and catchable AssertError semantics because a named buildType replaces dub's built-in unittest buildType; unlike check-unit it adds only PerfProbe.

check._comment: The ordinary-tests instrumented build: debug + --checkaction=C. `-C` turns a failed assert into an IMMEDIATE C abort() -- SIGABRT, before any stack unwinding -- which is the only reason the crash oracle can see an assert at all. With the default `-D` an AssertError kills the main thread while the process lives on, and every later HTTP request then costs the full 120 s command-bridge timeout (kCommandBridgeMaxIters=60_000 x 2 ms, http_server.d:79) before answering `timeout waiting for main thread`: the TEST hangs, the process does not. --boundscheck=on is carried for symmetry only and does NOTHING here -- measured: a debugMode build already traps an out-of-bounds @system index with or without it. Its value lives entirely in check-release below.

check-unit._comment: `check` MINUS --checkaction=C, PLUS the `unittests` build option, for `dub test --config=tests --build=check-unit` and for nothing else. Both halves are load-bearing. (1) The subtraction: ten sites under tests/unit/ assert that an assert raises a CATCHABLE AssertError (assertThrown!AssertError / catch (AssertError)); under --checkaction=C the binary SIGABRTs at the first of them and the whole module-unittest lane dies at once, which on an instrumented night reads like a sanitizer catastrophe rather than a build-flag mistake. (2) The addition: `--build=<name>` REPLACES dub's built-in `unittest` buildType wholesale rather than extending it, so a buildType without `unittests` compiles the test configuration WITHOUT -unittest -- measured, it fails outright with `module mesh_ops.extrude import g_vertexPosGridCandidates not found` and similar, because those symbols live behind version(unittest). Note also that `dub test` DEFAULTS to --build=unittest: a bare `dub test --config=tests` in the nightly lane would run an UNINSTRUMENTED binary all night and report health, so the lane passes --build=check-unit explicitly, and the preflight verifies EVERY binary the night executes -- including dub's own `vibe3d-test-tests`, not just ./vibe3d. Do not use this buildType to build the EDITOR: `unittests` there would run module unittests at startup.

check-release._comment: The shape of the shipped release, with the bounds checks put back -- the only build in which --boundscheck=on does any work at all. Measured on LDC 1.42.0 with an out-of-range @system index: -O0 traps with or without the flag; -O3 -release SILENTLY WRITES PAST THE END and prints the value back; -O3 -release --boundscheck=on traps again. So this buildType, and only this one, sees the class of defect that exists exclusively under optimisation. No --checkaction here: releaseMode compiles asserts out entirely, so the flag would be inert and its presence would imply otherwise.

sanitize._comment: AddressSanitizer. --fsanitize-address-use-after-return=never is NOT a performance choice: the shipped LDC 1.42 druntime is compiled WITHOUT version=SupportSanitizers (`nm libdruntime-ldc.a | grep FakeStack` is empty, though core/thread/threadbase.d does carry scanStackForASanFakeStack), so with use-after-return detection on, D's conservative GC cannot see stack roots that ASan moved to a fake stack -- lost roots, premature collection, memory corruption that looks like our bug. Pair it at RUN time with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=0. detect_leaks=0 belongs there too: SDL/assimp/ImGui allocate at startup and never free, and those are not our leaks. Honest limit of the method, which the phase-0 measurement did NOT shrink: the eight C/C++ wrapper dependencies and druntime/phobos all link PREBUILT and uninstrumented, so ASan sees our overruns of their buffers and our alloc/free mismatches (through the malloc interceptors) but nothing that happens INSIDE them.

sanitize-unit._comment: AddressSanitizer for the MODULE-UNITTEST binary -- `sanitize` plus the two differences that make it runnable there, both taken from `check-unit`'s measurements rather than by analogy. (1) `unittests` is ADDED because `--build=<name>` REPLACES dub's built-in `unittest` buildType wholesale, so without it `dub test --config=tests` compiles with no -unittest and fails outright. (2) `--checkaction=C` is DROPPED because ten sites under tests/unit/ assert that an assert raises a CATCHABLE AssertError; under -C the binary SIGABRTs at the first of them and the whole lane dies at once, which reads like a sanitizer catastrophe rather than a build-flag mistake. Everything else is `sanitize` verbatim, including --fsanitize-address-use-after-return=never, which is a CORRECTNESS requirement and not a speed choice: the shipped LDC druntime is built without version=SupportSanitizers, so with it on the conservative GC loses stack roots ASan moved to a fake stack. Pair at RUN time with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=0:detect_leaks=0. Honest limit, unchanged from `sanitize` and decisive for how a clean run must be read: the C/C++ dependencies, druntime and phobos link PREBUILT and uninstrumented, so a green run rules out an overrun in OUR code and says NOTHING about one inside theirs.

tsan._comment: ThreadSanitizer. Three parts of this are load-bearing and none is symmetry with `sanitize`. (1) version=SanitizerThreadPreinit pulls in source/tsan_preinit.d, WITHOUT WHICH THE BINARY DOES NOT REACH main: compiler-rt's tsan_preinit.cpp.o is never pulled out of libldc_rt.tsan.a (its only symbol is local), so the binary has no .preinit_array, so libcap.so.2's ELF constructor calls prctl() during _dl_init through a still-null REAL(prctl) and SIGSEGVs. Read out of a coredump under gdb; see that module's header. (2) --enable-asserts=false, AND NO --checkaction=C, and this pair is FORCED rather than chosen. The lane must run under --DRT-gcopt=gc:manual (see below). ManualGC.reserveArrayCapacity() returns 0 unconditionally (shipped source, manual/gc.d:283-286), and druntime's own _d_arraysetcapacity does `curCapacity = gc_reserveArrayCapacity(...); assert(curCapacity);` (capacity.d:181-182) -- so with asserts compiled in, ANY array.reserve() ABORTS THE PROCESS. The editor hit it during startup (_d_arraysetcapacity!(Param)) and never reached /api/registry. Measured four ways on a five-line program: debug + gc:manual dies with AssertError at capacity.d:182; -release + gc:manual and --enable-asserts=false + gc:manual both run and report capacity 0; debug + the ordinary collector reports capacity 1019. --enable-asserts=false is the surgical half of -release: bounds checks and debugInfo stay. --checkaction=C is then DROPPED rather than carried for symmetry, because with no asserts left to action it is inert and its presence would imply otherwise. The cost is stated rather than hidden: this lane cannot exercise ANY assert oracle, the validity asserts included -- that is `check`'s job, which is why it is a different buildType. A second cost follows from the same stub: reserve() silently yields capacity 0, so every append reallocates. (3) --boundscheck=on is deliberately NOT carried: it is measurably inert in a debugMode build (1410, M4), and symmetry with `check` is worth less than not implying a check that does nothing. RUN-TIME half, which lives in tools/sanitizer/lane.d's BuildTypeSpec and not in a workflow: the instance MUST run with --DRT-gcopt=gc:manual. Measured -- with the ordinary conservative GC, TSan deadlocks the process outright at >=2 allocating threads (thread_suspendAll parks in sem_wait while the other threads spin in an UNinstrumented SpinLock.lock(), so the stop-the-world signal is never acknowledged), and short of that it emits ~124 reports a minute, all of them GC memory REUSE that TSan cannot see freed. TSAN_OPTIONS must carry history_size=7 (without it reports arrive with no stack frames at all) and must NOT carry symbolize=0 (it silently disables suppression matching, which is by symbol NAME).

configurations.name: modeling
configurations._comment: Default. Modeling-only build — no IPR, no Cycles/RPR runtime, no D-Cycles/D-RadeonProRender dependencies. Fast compile, no extra system libs needed. All code under source/render/* and source/material/* is excluded from the build (gated by `version (WithRender)`). Includes the AI candidate ranker (version WithAI + d-onnxruntime).

configurations.name: modeling-noai
configurations._comment: AI-less modeling build (Windows 7 target). Same as `modeling` but WithAI is undefined and d-onnxruntime is NOT pulled in, so source/ai/onnx_backend.d compiles to an empty module and the statusline AI button renders as a disabled placeholder. The pure-D AI heuristics still compile but are unreachable (master switch stays off). Rationale: onnxruntime.dll statically imports api-ms-win-core-path-l1-1-0.dll (Windows 8+) — omitting it is the prerequisite for a binary that can load on Windows 7. CI's Win7 zip pairs this config with app-local UCRT + VC++ runtime DLLs.

configurations.name: with-render
configurations._comment: Opt-in build with two render backends (Cycles via D-Cycles, RPR via D-RadeonProRender) plus the AI ranker. The default `modeling` config never references the render repos so `dub build` works on machines that have neither. Git dependencies are pinned to commit SHAs so CI can reuse the persistent dub cache instead of re-cloning heavyweight repositories. For active backend development, register a local override once: `dub add-local ~/Code/D-RadeonProRender && dub add-local ~/Code/D-Cycles`. D-Cycles builds its C shim via CMake (Blender LFS submodule + optional CUDA/OptiX); D-RadeonProRender is dynamic-loaded bindbc. See doc/shader_framework_plan.md.

configurations.name: tests
configurations._comment-protocol-census: THE PREPARED-PROTOCOL CENSUS IS NOT GONE -- IT MOVED, and re-adding it here re-creates the cost it was moved out of. It used to be `preBuildCommands: ["python3 tools/check_prepared_protocol.py"]` on THIS configuration, put there by P1.0a's review for a real reason: without a caller, its whole-tree properties -- statement ORDER inside function bodies, caller sets across files nothing imports, occurrence counts, body digests -- could all drift under a green lane. The reason it could not stay: dub runs preBuildCommands on every build that actually builds, so every `dub test --config=tests` after any source edit paid the whole scan. Measured on the gate host 2026-09-02: 38.4 s wall / 243 MiB peak RSS for the scanner alone (the 3691 card's ~10 s had grown with it), against a `dub test` that is otherwise ~51 s. Task 4052 then found that 21.6 s of that was 72 compiler launches over `tests/compile_fail/`, deleted those fixtures in favour of `static assert(!__traits(isCopyable, T))` in tests/unit/prepared_tool_transition_test.d -- which THIS configuration pays for, and which is the right place for a property a compiler can state -- and the scanner alone now measures 19.5 s. Its caller is still `run_test.d`, the OTHER routine gate, as a barrier beside the test-liveness one, before anything is built: one payment per suite run instead of one per test build, and CI reaches it through `run_all.d --only unit`, which fans out to a FULL `./run_test.d`. `./run_test.d --check-protocol` runs it alone. If you are about to delete that call, read its comment there first.
configurations._comment-perf-portpolicy: Task 9220. tools/perf/lib/portpolicy.d decides which port the perf harness may clear and launch on (refuses a run_test.d worker window, derived from tools/harness/runslots.d, which rdmd reaches through the tracked symlink tools/perf/tools/harness/runslots.d). lib/lifecycle.d is compiled here only so tests/unit/perf_port_policy_test.d can pin, by type, that its kill and launch seams take an admitted PerfPort. Test-only, like the other tools/perf entries.
configurations._comment-hostspace: Task 5630. tools/harness/hostspace.d is the one owner of scratch-root and available-space policy for the standalone test runner and sanitizer lane. Both scripts import module tools.harness.hostspace; rdmd gives lane.d only tools/sanitizer as its import root, so the tracked file symlink under that root preserves absolute-script invocation from a foreign cwd. The real file is listed explicitly in sourceFiles, which keeps it test-only: modeling and with-render do not compile harness policy. importPaths still repeats source because declaring this array replaces dub's derived default.
configurations._comment-perf-vslast: Task 2420. `tools/perf/lib/vslast.d` is the nightly perf gate's DECISION -- the part that can be wrong -- and it is pulled into THIS configuration alone so that its witness (tests/unit/perf_vslast_gate_test.d) runs in a gate lane instead of nowhere. tools/perf is an rdmd unit with no place in either lane otherwise (tools/perf/README.md D1 says so), which is why it carried zero unittests before. The module is deliberately dependency-free -- plain doubles and strings, no HistoryEntry, no lib.history -- so task 2420 itself adds only this file; task 1460 separately adds baseline.d + stats.d for the debt-ledger witness named by the adjacent comment. `importPaths` must repeat "source" because naming it at all REPLACES the default dub derives from sourcePaths; "tools/perf" is what makes the files' declared `module lib.*` names match their paths. Do NOT move either key to the root or to `modeling`: the editor build has no business importing perf-harness code, and the explicit-file boundary is what keeps that true.
configurations._comment-perf-ledger: The two `tools/perf/lib` modules are compiled INTO this configuration on purpose (task 1460). The perf debt ledger's law -- `judge` / `debtImproved` / `reconcileDebt` in `lib.baseline` -- is pure arithmetic over recorded numbers, so it must be provable without launching vibe3d, and `dub test --config=tests` only looks at these source paths. `tools/perf/run.d` itself stays OUT: it is a script with a `main()`, not a library. Nothing here reaches a shipped binary -- `modeling` / `modeling-noai` / `with-render` carry neither entry, and dub merges configuration settings on top of the root rather than the other way round (see _comment-sourcepaths).
configurations._comment: The module-unittest gate (task 0706): `dub test --config=tests`. It exists so unittest blocks have somewhere to live OTHER than source/ -- measured by audit 4, 25% of source/ was test code and the god-files were 48-96% tests, with no lever to shrink them while the only source path was `source`. See tests/unit/README.md for what may move there.
configurations._comment-name: The name is `tests` and NOT `unittest`, and that is load-bearing. dub gives a configuration literally named `unittest` a special branch: it uses that configuration VERBATIM and skips its own test-main injection. Measured here on dub 1.41 -- with the name `unittest`, `dub test` printed `Linking vibe3d` / `Running vibe3d`: it built the EDITOR with -unittest, overwrote ./vibe3d (the binary `run_test.d --no-build` reuses), ran the unittest blocks, and then whether it terminated at all depended on druntime returning runMain=false. Under any other name dub injects dub_test_root.d, builds a separate `vibe3d-test-<config>` binary, leaves ./vibe3d alone, and -- the part that matters most for this task -- `static import`s EVERY module of the target, which is what guarantees a tests/unit/ module that nothing imports still registers its ModuleInfo and actually runs. Cost of not using the magic name: a bare `dub test` falls back to the default configuration (`modeling`) and silently omits tests/unit/. That is why every caller passes --config=tests explicitly; a wrong one is visible in the run's own output as `Running vibe3d-test-modeling` and a lower `N modules passed unittests`.
configurations._comment-sourcepaths: All fourteen production owners compile directly under root unittest flags in one compiler target, preserving private blocks. Desktop and all thirteen package public test roots register through the generated test main. Test-only sourceLibrary selections prevent package D archive links; native and external archives remain declared.
configurations._comment-duplication: `WithAI` + d-onnxruntime are copied from `modeling` rather than hoisted to the root ON PURPOSE: `modeling-noai` deliberately omits both (Windows 7 target -- onnxruntime.dll needs Win8+ APIs), so hoisting them would silently un-do that build. Keep this block in sync with `modeling` by hand; there are only two lines of it.

configurations.name: web
configurations._comment: The browser build's SEAM KEY, declared so it is DERIVED and not hand-passed. Measured 2026-09-21: `web` is predefined by no compiler and appeared in no dub version list, so every `version (web)` site across the wave-15 seams took the NATIVE arm on a wasm target. One slice's own wasm control went green only because its harness passed -d-version=web itself, which witnesses the flag rather than the build. `WebAssembly` IS compiler-predefined on a wasm triple, so sites on it fire on ANY wasm target -- a superset of this one. The two are different predicates: a fact about the target versus a decision about the build.
configurations._comment-deps: No d-onnxruntime, nfde, or bindbc-assimp6 here: those families are version-gated out of this build, so the dependencies would be pulled for code that is not compiled. The wasm-only link settings name archives built by tools/build_web_native_deps.sh; the platform suffix keeps a native dub build --config=web on its existing native dependency set. d-stb-image already contributes stb_image_c on posix/wasm, so putting this web directory first makes that name resolve to the Emscripten archive.
